title: lokyr/blocks
description: The commands' blocks: the command's header across the top of a pane, of the command whose output the view shows, its button to the block's end, the blocks' dividers and a failed block's tint.

background.description: The theme's token of the pill's background, by its name, as "panel.bg" or "accent".
background.x-guide:
The theme's tokens of the header's colors, by their names: the pill's background, its text, its border, the line across the pane, and the color over the pill's background under the pointer.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| a token's name, as `"accent"`, `"panel.bg"`, `"field.bg"` or `"text.secondary"` | `"panel.bg"`, `"text"`, `"panel.border"`, `"panel.border"`, `"button.hover.bg"` |

- The tokens are those of the theme in force, as a theme's `[interface]` names them, and each follows the light and the dark appearance; a name that the theme lacks takes the color of its name without its last part, as `panel` for `panel.foo`, then none.
- `border = "accent"` draws the pill's border in the theme's accent.
- They apply at once, as you save the file, to a header that shows too.
background.x-example-comment: the theme's token of the pill's background, by its name

text.description: The theme's token of the pill's text, by its name.
text.x-example-comment: the theme's token of its text

border.description: The theme's token of the pill's border, by its name.
border.x-example-comment: the theme's token of its border, as "accent"

line.description: The theme's token of the hairline across the pane, by its name.
line.x-example-comment: the theme's token of the line across the pane

hover.description: The theme's token of the pill's background under the pointer, over its own, by its name.
hover.x-example-comment: the theme's token over its background under the pointer

font-size.description: The size of the header's text, in the terminal's font, in points; 0, or none, for the terminal's own size.
font-size.x-guide:
The size of the header's text, which takes the terminal's font, as [`[font]`](#font) names it.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| points, from `0` to `200`; `0` for the terminal's own size | `0` |

- Of the terminal's own size, the pill is about a row of the terminal high, its padding past it; a smaller size keeps it within the row.
- It applies at once, as you save the file, to a header that shows too.
font-size.x-example-comment: points, 0 to 200, of the terminal's font; 0 for its own size

font-weight.description: The weight of the header's text, of the terminal's font's faces, the nearest that it has; regular is the terminal's own face.
font-weight.x-guide:
The weight of the header's text, of the terminal's font's faces, the nearest that it has.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`, `heavy` | `regular` |

- `regular` is the terminal's own face, as [`style`](#style) names it; the others the family's faces nearest to their weights, which a family of a single weight does not have.
- It applies at once, as you save the file, to a header that shows too.
font-weight.x-example-comment: light | regular | medium | semibold | bold | heavy

padding-x.description: The room left and right of the text in the pill, in points.
padding-x.x-guide:
The room in the pill around its text, in points: left and right, and above and below.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| `padding-x` from `0` to `40`; `padding-y` from `0` to `20` | `8`, `1` |

- The pill's ends stay round, of half its height.
- They apply at once, as you save the file, to a header that shows too.
padding-x.x-example-comment: points, 0 to 40, left and right of the text

padding-y.description: The room above and below the text in the pill, in points.
padding-y.x-example-comment: points, 0 to 20, above and below it

align.description: Where the header's pill sits along the hairline across the pane: a little in from its left, in its middle, or a little in from its right.
align.x-guide:
Where the header's pill sits along the line across the pane.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| `left`, `center`, `right` | `left` |

- `left` and `right` keep it a little in from the pane's edge; `center` in the pane's middle.
- It applies at once, as you save the file, to a header that shows too.
align.x-example-comment: left | center | right: where its pill sits along the line

max-length.description: The most characters of the command's line that the header shows, the line cut at its end of an ellipsis beyond them.
max-length.x-guide:
The most characters of the command's line that the header shows.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| characters, from `1` to `1000` | `80` |

- A longer line is cut at its end of an ellipsis, `…`; its tooltip, and what VoiceOver reads, keep it whole.
- Whatever its length, the pill stays within the pane, its line cut of an ellipsis where the pane is narrower.
- It applies at once, as you save the file, to a header that shows too.
max-length.x-example-comment: characters, 1 to 1000, of the line, cut of … beyond them

dividers.description: Whether a hairline divides each command's block from the one before, at the top of its first row, across the pane.
dividers.x-guide:
Whether a thin line divides each command's block from the one before.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| `true`, `false` | `true` |

- The line sits at the top of each block's first row, its prompt's, across the pane, the prompt where you type too.
- Its color is the theme's `blocks.divider`, as the interface's lines by default.
- The gutter's bar of each command runs along its block, from its prompt to its output's end, while Blocks runs, whatever this key.
- It applies at once, as you save the file.

failed-tint.description: Whether the rows of a block whose command failed are tinted, across the pane, besides the gutter's red bar.
failed-tint.x-guide:
Whether the rows of a block whose command failed are tinted, across the pane.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| `true`, `false` | `false` |

- A command fails of an exit status other than 0, as an interrupted command does.
- By default a failed block shows the gutter's red bar alone; `true` tints its rows too, of the theme's `blocks.failed`, a faint red by default.
- It applies at once, as you save the file.

header.description: How the header of the block whose output the pane's top shows looks: the block's prompt rows themselves, pinned at the pane's top, or a pill of its command line on a line across the pane.
header.x-guide:
How the header of the block whose output the pane's top shows looks.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `pill` | `rows` |

- `rows` pins the block's own prompt rows at the pane's top as soon as the prompt's first row scrolls above it, its prompt and its command line as your shell drew them, three rows at most, over the rows that scroll under them, with a line under them; a click on them scrolls to the prompt.
- `pill` shows the command line in a pill on a line across the pane, of the keys above, with an arrow to the block's end.
- It applies at once, as you save the file.
header.x-example-comment: rows | pill: the prompt's rows pinned, or a pill of the command line

spacing.description: Whether a blank row comes before each prompt that follows a command, as room between the blocks, the divider drawn through its middle.
spacing.x-guide:
Whether a blank row comes before each prompt that follows a command, as room between the blocks.

| Values | Default |
|---|---|
| `true`, `false` | `false` |

- Lokyr puts the blank row there itself as the prompt starts, in any shell that marks its prompts, so your shell's config needs nothing.
- The divider between the blocks runs through the middle of the blank row, and a selected block's tint reaches it.
- No blank row comes before the first prompt, after an empty line, or at the top of a cleared screen.
- It applies at once, from the next prompt, as you save the file; the blank rows already there stay when you turn it off.

x-guide:
<sub>Platforms: macOS</sub>

The commands' blocks of the built-in plugin `lokyr/blocks`: each command that the shell marks, its prompt, its line and its output, is a block. As soon as the first row of a block's prompt scrolls above the view, the block's prompt rows stay pinned at the pane's top, which a click scrolls to the command's prompt, or, of `header = "pill"`, a pill of the command as you typed it, in the terminal's font, sits on a thin line across the pane's top, over its first row, which a click scrolls to the command's prompt; while the view does not show the block's end, an arrow beside the pill scrolls there, the output's last row at the view's bottom, or the screen of a command that still runs. Its colors are the theme's, of the tokens that its keys name, so that they follow the light and the dark appearance. A thin line divides the blocks, the gutter's bar of each command runs along its block, the block that a click or the keyboard selects is tinted, and a failed block's rows can be tinted. A blank row before each prompt can make room between the blocks.

`lokyr/blocks` replaces `lokyr/command-header`, the plain header, of the same keys, which comes back while `lokyr/blocks` is off: keys of `[plugins.command-header]` apply then, and the settings window notes it above them while `lokyr/blocks` runs.
